ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier), Articles L.561-1 to L.561-60 and R.561-1 et seq. (AML/CFT and beneficial-owner register); Directive (EU) 2015/849 and Directive (EU) 2018/843 as transposed by Ordonnance No. 2020-115 of 12 February 2020 and Décret No. 2020-118 of 12 February 2020; beneficial-owner register (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs, RBE) governed by Articles L.561-46 to L.561-53 CMF and Décret No. 2016-567 of 25? and Décret No. 2016-567 of 24 April 2016 as amended; French Commercial Code (Code de commerce) Articles L.123-10 to L.123-33 (RCS) and L.223-1 et seq. (SARL); Loi PACTE No. 2019-486 and Décret No. 2021-1011 establishing the Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) operated by INPI since 31 December 2022.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national ID of every manager (gérant) and every beneficial owner holding 25% or more of capital, voting rights or ultimate control
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or consular authority of the country of origin (notarially certified copy)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Convention of 5 October 1961) for non-EU Convention States; French consular legalization (légalisation consulaire) for non-Convention States; EU/EEA official documents benefit from the simplified procedures of EU Regulation 2016/1191

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / police clearance (extrait de casier judiciaire or equivalent) for each non-resident manager and, where available, each UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent criminal-record or judicial authority of the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the competent authority of the State of origin; French consular legalization for non-Hague States

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified French translation of all foreign-language documents (passports, corporate certificates, registers, powers of attorney and address proof)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Sworn translator approved by a French Cour d'appel (expert judiciaire) or equivalent notarized translation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The translation is certified by the sworn translator; the underlying original document must separately bear the Hague Apostille or consular legalization, as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / current extract of the company register (or equivalent RNE-type extract) of any corporate shareholder or corporate UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry / registrar of companies in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the issuing authority of the State of origin (generally Ministry of Justice or Ministry of Foreign Affairs); French consular legalization where the State is not a Hague Convention member

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of address (utility bill or bank statement dated within three months) for each manager and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Originating bank, utility provider or municipal authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille is not normally required for address proof; a certified French translation and an official institution stamp or letterhead are required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming banking history and expected payment rails (SWIFT LC / TT Wire) for non-resident contributors to share capital
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing credit institution in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: On bank letterhead with official bank seal; a Hague Apostille is additionally required only where the letter evidences funds in excess of the applicable French AML declaration threshold or where the bank is located in a FATF non-compliant jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Below is duplicate key, must be omitted.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises operated by INPI (https://formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr); official name-availability and corporate register data at https://data.inpi.fr; ancillary search via Infogreffe covering the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All incorporation filings must be in French under Article L.123-12-2 of the French Commercial Code and Law No. 94-665 of 4 August 1994 on the use of the French language. The corporate name (dénomination sociale) may contain Latin-script foreign words or a registered foreign trademark only if the name is not contrary to French public order and is not misleading; any non-Latin-script name must be transliterated into Latin script and each attached foreign-language document must be accompanied by a certified French translation.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque, Établissement de crédit, Finance, Assurance, Réassurance, Gestion d'actifs (regulated financial terms requiring prior ACPR or ministerial clearance or otherwise prohibited)
République, Nation, Ministère, Préfecture, Mairie, Service public, Police, Gendarmerie (misleading public-authority terms)
Avocat, Notaire, Expert-comptable, Huissier, Médecin, Pharmacien, Vétérinaire (protected regulated professions)
SA, SAS, SCA, SNC, GIE, EURL, SCI (alternative legal-form suffixes that misrepresent the SARL form being registered)
Croix-Rouge, ONU, UNESCO, Ambassade, Fédération, Université, Académie, Institut National (terms suggesting state patronage or international institutional affiliation)
France, Paris, République française (combinations falsely implying official approval, state sponsorship or public administrative endorsement)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: No statutory pre-registration name-reservation system exists for a French SARL equivalent to common-law jurisdictions; the 30-day window reflects the practical validity of a pre-filing distinctiveness check on data.inpi.fr before a new declaration must be made. Procedure on rejection: (1) the registrar issues a written decision of rejection (décision de rejet) stating the grounds under the distinctive-name rules; (2) within 30 days of notification, the applicant may file a free administrative appeal (recours gracieux) with the INPI business-formalities directorate or, where the refusal originates from the greffe du tribunal de commerce, a hierarchical appeal (recours hiérarchique) to the competent commercial registry, attaching a corrected name and arguments distinguishing it from prior registrations; (3) if the administrative appeal is unsuccessful, an action for excess of power (recours pour excès de pouvoir) may be filed with the Tribunal administratif within two months, or an urgent interim order (référé) may be sought before the President of the commercial court under Article R.123-130 of the French Commercial Code where the refusal causes imminent harm; (4) the most efficient commercial remedy is to file a fresh registration request with an amended and distinguishable name and, if the brand is essential, to register the mark with INPI (10-year term) to obtain priority. No extension of the 30-day validity window is available; after 30 days a new name availability check is required.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible subject to strict statutory limits: under Articles L.123-11-1 and L.123-11-2 of the French Commercial Code, an SARL may establish its registered office at the premises of a licensed domiciliation company (domiciliataire agréé) under a written domiciliation agreement, provided the arrangement does not create a fictitious office and the company's real central administration, management decisions and operational substance remain attributable to France. A pure mail-forwarding post-box without any management presence or business records in France is not accepted for a manufacturer in ISIC 2811 and would expose the company to recharacterization as an abuse of law, the voidness of the registered-office clause, and joint liability of the domiciliataire under Article L.123-11-4 of the Commercial Code.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium-to-High: approximately 35% probability of at least one unannounced physical or documentary inspection within the first 24 months of operation. DGFiP (tax), URSSAF (social contributions), DREETS (labour and RSE), DGDDI (customs where outboard engines are exported outside the EU) and INPI/RNE delegated officers may verify the reality of commercial substance, including premises, marine-engine inventory, machinery, staff presence and corporate records. Registration at a virtual-office address increases the estimated inspection probability by an additional 15% and materially raises substance-challenge risk.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RNE incorporation filing and statutory registration fee paid via the Guichet unique (SARL formation)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: INPI (Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fixed tariff set by ministerial arrêté of 28 September 2022 (€53.47 converted at approximately 1.085 EUR/USD)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal announcement of incorporation in a licensed legal gazette (annonce légale de constitution)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Private legal-gazette publisher (journal d'annonces légales) licensed in the département of the registered office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated rate per character with market benchmark of €145–€165 for a standard SARL constitution announcement

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of articles of association (statuts) by French-speaking corporate counsel including AML/UBO compliance annex
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External French law firm (not legally mandatory but market practice for non-resident founders)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of €750–€1,000 plus VAT for a standard cash-contribution SARL statute package

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified French translation of foreign corporate documents and assembly of the apostille/consular legalization bundle
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Court-appointed sworn translator and the competent authorities of the States of origin
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of €50–€70 per page for certified translation plus €15–€25 per apostille stamp

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered-office domiciliation agreement (virtual office) covering the first year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed domiciliation company (domiciliataire agréé) or law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of €20–€35 per month for commercial-premises domiciliation satisfying Article L.123-11-1 of the French Commercial Code

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation AML/KYC screening of all UBOs and managers against EU, UN, French and OFAC sanctions lists, including PEP and negative-media checks
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: ACPR-supervised corporate service provider or specialized compliance screening platform
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of €150–€220 per entity screening package with documented audit trail and retention records

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Opening of the French business bank account and purchase of statutory corporate books and company seal
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French credit institution and authorized stationery supplier
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank account opening benchmark of €80–€250; statutory registers and seal benchmark of €50–€80

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Preparation and submission of the beneficial-owner declaration (RBE) as part of the registration bundle
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Legal practitioner preparing the RBE annex (filing tariff itself is absorbed in the INPI registration fee)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Marginal professional preparation cost of €30–€50 reflecting the administrative time for UBO identification and certification

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 and R.223-1 to R.223-36; Civil Code Articles 1832 et seq.; beneficial-owner rules under Commercial Code Articles L.561-46 et seq.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI), with registration in the Registre du commerce et des sociétés (RCS) maintained by the competent commercial-court registry (greffe du tribunal de commerce).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Electronic declaration of company formation (formalité de constitution) submitted through the INPI Guichet unique, including the SARL articles of association, beneficial-owner declaration, and supporting corporate and premises documents.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital applies; capital may be set at EUR 1 or any higher amount. For cash contributions, at least 20% of subscribed capital must be paid on incorporation and the balance within five years of registration. Funds must be deposited with an authorized bank, notary, or Caisse des dépôts et consignations, and released after registration upon presentation of the Kbis extract. The stated USD fee is an approximate conversion of the standard RCS filing fee and excludes publication, beneficial-owner filing, translation, and other ancillary charges.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The sole shareholder or shareholders of [Company Name] SARL resolve to approve and adopt the articles of association, subscribe for the entire issued capital in the proportions recorded in the subscription schedule, and confirm payment of the required initial cash contributions into the company formation account. The registered office is established at [full French address]. [Name] is appointed gérant for an indefinite term, with authority to manage and represent the company within the limits of French law and the articles. The gérant is authorized to complete all registration, tax, banking, beneficial-owner, and licensing formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm shareholders, management, activities, and registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique and the competent commercial-court registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the legal name, purpose, share capital, shareholder percentages, gérant, financial year, registered office, and principal activity. Verify that the registered office is legally available and that the premises permit the stated manufacturing activity. Foreign shareholders and managers should provide legalized or apostilled corporate and identity documents where applicable, together with certified French translations.
required_dossiers: Foreign corporate shareholder certificate of incorporation and current good-standing or registry extract
Registered-office title, lease, domiciliation agreement, or host declaration
Description of business activities and principal establishment
Manager declaration of non-conviction and parentage details
Power of attorney, if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct inconsistent names, addresses, activity codes, translations, or identity data before submission. Obtain a replacement registry extract or updated legalized document where validity is questioned.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute the articles and subscribe the capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized bank, notary, or Caisse des dépôts et consignations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the articles of association and subscription schedule. Open a temporary formation account and deposit at least 20% of cash contributions. Obtain the certificate of deposit. Contributions in kind require valuation by a commissaire aux apports unless the statutory exemption conditions are satisfied and the shareholders assume the applicable valuation risk.
required_dossiers: Independent contribution valuation report, if required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Resolve bank compliance queries with ownership charts, source-of-funds evidence, certified translations, and manager identification. If a valuation report is defective, appoint a replacement commissaire aux apports and amend the subscription documentation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized Journal of Legal Notices (journal d'annonces légales) in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish the statutory formation notice containing the company name, legal form, capital, registered office, purpose, duration, gérant identity, and relevant registration information. Retain the publication certificate for the INPI filing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Republish a corrected notice if mandatory particulars are omitted or inaccurate and upload the corrected certificate with the filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the electronic formation application and beneficial-owner declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create the company formation application, select SARL, identify the principal activity under the applicable French NAF classification, upload all supporting documents, submit the beneficial-owner declaration, pay the applicable charges, and digitally sign the filing. The INPI transmits the information to the RCS, tax administration, social authorities, and other relevant bodies.
required_dossiers: Manager declaration of non-conviction and parentage
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond through the INPI dashboard within the stated cure period. Upload corrected or missing documents, pay any additional charge, and resubmit the queried item. If rejected, request clarification from the competent greffe and file an amended application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain registration evidence and activate the company
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Competent commercial-court registry, INPI, tax administration, and social-security authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the SIREN, SIRET, APE/NAF classification, and Kbis extract. Present the Kbis and bank deposit certificate to release the capital. Convert the temporary account into the operating account, establish accounting records, register for VAT where required, and complete employer and payroll registrations before hiring personnel.
required_dossiers: VAT registration or tax identification correspondence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request correction of registry data through the INPI or competent greffe. Notify the tax or social authority separately where an inter-administration transmission has failed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt post-incorporation governance and compliance records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company records maintained at the registered office; tax and social authorities as applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Maintain the articles, shareholder register, capital subscription evidence, gérant appointment, beneficial-owner evidence, accounting books, and minutes. Document related-party arrangements, delegations, bank mandates, insurance, product compliance, and annual accounts approval. For a SARL, the gérant manages and represents the company; a statutory board is not required.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify defective minutes or registers promptly, document ratification by the competent shareholder body, and submit any required amended filing or annual disclosure.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement (DREAL) and the Préfecture of the department where the facility is located. The competent mairie handles planning and building matters.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No general manufacturing licence is normally required for marine outboard-engine manufacture. An Installation Classée pour la Protection de l'Environnement (ICPE) declaration, registration, or environmental authorization may be required depending on installed capacities, combustion equipment, surface-treatment operations, fuel and hazardous-material storage, waste activities, and emissions.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for Ecological Transition, administered locally through the competent DREAL and the Préfecture
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Site-specific. The facility must be screened against the ICPE nomenclature and the Environmental Code. It may be exempt from ICPE formalities, subject to declaration, subject to registration, or subject to full environmental authorization and environmental assessment. A full EIA is not automatically required solely because the activity is engine manufacturing.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Comply with the applicable ICPE ministerial or prefectural prescriptions, Environmental Code requirements, wastewater discharge authorization, hazardous-waste traceability, storage controls, and workplace chemical rules. Control VOCs from coatings and solvents, combustion emissions, noise, oil and fuel releases, and wastewater. Discharges must meet the applicable permit limits; hazardous waste must be transferred to authorized operators with required tracking documentation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain any required planning or building permit from the mairie, consult the Service départemental d'incendie et de secours (SDIS) on fire prevention and emergency access, and complete fire-protection, evacuation, hazardous-material storage, electrical, lifting-equipment, pressure-equipment, and structural-load inspections as applicable. Occupational compliance is supervised by the Inspection du travail and the relevant occupational-health service. No single universal pre-opening workplace clearance applies, but mandatory risk assessments, safety documentation, employee training, and equipment inspections must be completed before operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) — impots.gouv.fr professional portal 'Espace Professionnel' for corporate income tax and TVA/VAT filings; business incorporation and tax registration formalities via the Guichet Unique des Formalités d'Entreprises operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI); customs and export controls via the Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI / douane.gouv.fr).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 — Incorporate the SARL through the Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr): issuance of SIREN/SIRET (INSEE) and automatic allocation of the intra-Community French VAT number (format FR + 14 characters) upon statutory registration. Step 2 — Activate the corporate tax account with the local Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) and enrol in the professional 'Espace Pro' for filing corporation tax (impôt sur les sociétés) and VAT (TVA). Step 3 — Foreign entities without a French establishment must either (i) register directly with the dedicated SIE des non-résidents, appoint a fiscal representative if established outside the EU, and obtain a direct French VAT number where a French taxable nexus or permanent establishment arises, or (ii) use the EU One-Stop-Shop (OSS/IOSS) for distance sales and qualifying B2B services, which avoids full local entity registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — a standard commercial SARL is by default subject to corporation tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS) under Articles 206(1) and 209 CGI regardless of profit distribution; the entity is a separate taxable person for corporate income tax and VAT, and shareholders are taxed only upon distributions. Flow-through/transparent treatment is reserved to specific opt-in cases (e.g., family SARL under Article 239 bis AA CGI).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: French law has no US-style 'check-the-box'; entity classification derives from legal form. Available elections: (1) SARL de famille — option for partnership-style transparency (Article 239 bis AA CGI) where all members are spouses or same-family relatives; (2) option for corporation tax by otherwise transparent partnerships (Article 206(3) CGI) — not relevant for a standard SARL; (3) fiscal integration ('intégration fiscale') election under Article 223 A CGI for groups holding ≥95% subsidiaries; (4) exit-tax deferral election (Article 167 bis CGI). Hybrid mismatch outcomes are non-elective: French ATAD implementation (Article 212 bis CGI) automatically denies deductions for hybrid mismatch transactions; no elective hybrid regime is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée — TVA); Code Général des Impôts Articles 256 ff.; EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: None (EUR 0) — established French suppliers and manufacturers must register for VAT from the first taxable transaction; the only de minimis rule is the EU-wide EUR 10,000 annual distance-sales ceiling (Directive 2006/112/EC) for cross-border EU B2C supplies, above which French VAT must be charged via OSS or local registration; non-established foreign sellers with French B2C nexus must register via the SIE non-résidents or use OSS/IOSS and enjoy no domestic exemption threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France applies a semi-deferred clearance model (no real-time stamping): under Loi de finances 2023, ordonnance n° 2024-316 and décret n° 2024-708, all domestic B2B invoices must be issued and received in structured electronic form through a certified Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire (PDP) or the public Portail Public de Facturation (PPF); B2C and international transaction data must be reported electronically through the same channel. Mandatory implementation dates: 1 September 2026 for large companies (grandes entreprises) and mid-caps (ETI), 1 September 2027 for small and medium enterprises (PME/TPE). API integration between accounting/e-invoicing systems and the chosen PDP is required; accepted syntaxes include Factur-X, UBL and CII; no per-invoice fiscal authorisation or digital stamping is applied.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available under Article 262-1 CGI for tangible goods sold by the taxpayer and physically transported or dispatched outside the EU, provided transport is evidenced and goods leave EU territory within 90 days of delivery (administrative tolerance). Article 262 ter CGI zero-rates intra-EU B2B supplies when the purchaser communicates a valid EU VAT number and the EC Sales List obligation is fulfilled. Offshore services are zero-rated only where (i) supplied to a customer established outside the EU, (ii) directly related to exported goods (e.g., transport, handling, processing, repair) under Article 261 C-1-2 CGI, or (iii) place-of-supply rules (Articles 259–259 D CGI) locate the transaction outside French territorial VAT. Domestic sales of light diesel outboard engines remain taxable at 20%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration lodged via DELTA (Déclaration d'exportation with MRN — Movement Reference Number) evidencing exit from the EU
Transport document: Bill of Lading (sea), Air Waybill (air) or CMR (road) proving physical export
Commercial invoice (facture commerciale) and packing list matching the customs declaration in value, quantity and tariff classification
Inward Remittance Certificate — SWIFT MT103 or bank credit advice proving receipt of export proceeds in convertible currency and reconciling to invoice value
Export contract, purchase order and Incoterms/insurance evidence (including letter of credit where used) supporting commercial substance
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGFiP and DGDDI jointly audit export zero-rating claims; where export evidence is missing, false or irreconcilable, the 0% rate is retroactively clawed back and 20% VAT becomes immediately payable, plus: (i) late-payment interest (intérêts de retard) of 0.20% per month (Article 1727 CGI); (ii) 40% penalty for deliberate understatement (manquement délibéré) or 80% for fraud/abuse of law (Article 1729 CGI); (iii) criminal tax-fraud exposure under Article 1741 CGI — up to 3 years' imprisonment and a EUR 75,000 fine (aggravated to 7 years/EUR 250,000 for organised fraud or laundering); (iv) customs penalties for false export declarations under the Code des Douanes — fines up to half to twice the value of the goods plus confiscation; and (v) extension of the statute-of-limitations to a 10-year re-opening window for undisclosed fraud (Article L.186 Livre des Procédures Fiscales). Supporting records must be retained for at least six years and presented on official demand.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) as the designated central bank and foreign-exchange reporting authority, acting jointly with the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury) for exchange-market policy and with the French Ministry of Economy, Finance and Industrial Sovereignty for investment controls.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is part of the Economic and Monetary Union; the euro is fully convertible for both current-account and capital-account transactions. No exchange-control authorizations are required for ordinary trade, capital injections, or dividend remittances. Profit remittances to non-resident shareholders are subject solely to applicable corporate withholding tax (EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive reduces to 0% where qualifying; otherwise domestic law withholding up to 30%, often reduced by treaty), and such payments can be executed freely through a bank wire upon approval of the corporate accounts and declaration of the dividend. The current account is fully liberalized under EU Treaty obligations, and capital movements are unrestricted except for a narrow, prior-authorization screening of foreign direct investments in defence/security sectors under Article L151-3 of the French Monetary and Financial Code.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement or mandatory conversion ratio in France. Exporters may retain and freely manage euro or foreign-currency proceeds, hold foreign-currency clearing accounts, and use them for payments or hedging. The sole obligation is statistical: cross-border transactions must be recorded for Banque de France balance-of-payments reporting, ordinarily through the credit intermediary or via a direct corporate statement for large or significant flows (e.g., direct investment aggregating above the applicable Banque de France reporting threshold).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds: Notice: no surrender or liquidation obligation applies in the Eurozone for non-resident exporters operating through a French SARL.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account - Compte Séquestre / Operational Account (IBAN FR76)
Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account (IBAN FR76)
Operational Account / Treasury and Trade Solutions

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for transactional euro clearing and FX payments; Low for core treasury and trade-finance instruments. A PSD2-licensed Electronic Money Institution in the EEA may open a business payment account with an IBAN, execute SEPA/wire-style transfers, and offer limited FX contracts, but it cannot independently issue commercial letters of credit, provide documentary collections, structure cross-currency swaps, or extend liquidity facilities. These products require a fully-regulated credit institution. Legal constraints include requirement under PSD2 to segregate client funds, unavailability of Banque de France refinancing access, and lack of supervision as a credit institution; therefore the SARL's primary treasury architecture should rest on a tier-1 French bank, with an EMI used only for alternative collection/operational flow in low-risk markets.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under French AML/KYC regulation (Code Monétaire et Financier Art. L561-5) and EU AMLD4/5, the SARL's legal representative, beneficial owner(s), and authorized signatories must be positively identified. Remote opening is technically permissible where the bank accepts PVID video-identity technology and qualified electronic signatures, but in practice for a newly formed SARL with a non-resident parent and manufacturing scope, compliance officers commonly require at least one physical attendance at a French branch or a meeting with the banking compliance officer, or an alternative via notarially certified POA/passport certification at a French consulate. A structured KYC dossier is mandatory; the default expectation is that directors, if non-resident, must appear physically or by secure e-meeting with a notarized identity verification before a French-licensed authority.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident parent company injecting subscribed capital without an auditable board resolution and supporting funds-origin trail
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized capital subscription minutes, SARL statuts (articles of association), bank statement evidencing transfer from the parent's corporate account, updated shareholders' register, register of beneficial owners, and Kbis extraction from the French Commercial Registry (RCS).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owner identity mismatch or lack of transparent corporate ownership (e.g., bearer shares, multi-tier holding)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Beneficial Ownership Declaration form (Formulaire BE) filed with the Registre des Titulaires, passport/NIE/Titre de séjour, apostilled birth certificates, certificate of good standing for parent entities, and complete organizational chart to ultimate natural persons.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Wire payment for marine outboard engine exports originating from a restrictive sanctions-heavy or high-risk jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial purchase order, final invoice, bill of lading, engine serial number register, marine insurance certificate, raw-material procurement invoices, internal EU/US/UN sanctions screening report, and bank reference letter from the shipper's correspondent bank.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity capital injection for the French SARL is fully liberalized and does not require prior Banque de France authorization unless the activity falls under Article R151-3 foreign-investment screening (defence/security or sensitive technology). The compliant wire routing is a SWIFT MT103 from the parent corporate account to the SARL's French IBAN, with the payment defined as 'Direct Investment – Equity Capital Contribution' and the transfer instruction including the corporate purpose code equal to 'Foreign Direct Investment' / category 'Equity Injection'. The receiving French bank, as an authorized financial intermediary, records the statistical balance-of-payments (Ifib/FCIR) reporting automatically. Where the aggregate annual direct-investment flow exceeds the Bank's applicable direct reporting threshold (currently EUR 15 million per the French rule), the SARL or its intermediary must file the prescribed Banque de France declaration using form 'Établissement direct' within 20 days of the operation. Verification is made by ensuring the remitter is the real beneficial parent, the amount matches the capital subscription resolution, and the SARL files the capital increase with the RCS and official publication.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for trade settlements follow: (1) for EUR payments to EEA counterparties, SEPA Credit Transfer; (2) for non-EEA or USD/CNY/other currencies, SWIFT MT103 wire transfers routed through the French bank's correspondent network; (3) for documentary marine-engine deliveries, a commercial Letter of Credit issued by the buyer's bank may be settled under SWIFT MT700/MT710 with presentation of a full documents set including bill of lading, commercial invoice, Fumigation Certificate, Marine Insurance Certificate, engine inspection certificate, and certificate of origin. For significant euro liquidity, TARGET2 is the RTGS clearing rail; SWIFT FIN remains the standard messaging protocol. The SARL should establish a dedicated clearing account at a tier-1 bank, use a single gateway for all outward payments to ensure efficient know-your-counterparty and sanctions screening, and record all cross-border FX flows under the relevant Banque de France statement or via the bank's transaction-reporting facility.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain vanilla foreign-exchange forwards on EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CNH with an authorized French credit institution, limited to documentary underlying trade exposure.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on currencies with convertibility restrictions, permitted where the SARL has a genuine trade or balance-sheet exposure in that currency and where the NDF is entered with an authorised counterparty under EMIR.
Cross-currency swaps addressing long-dated EUR/foreign-currency cash-flow mismatches from international contracts, subject to EMIR collateralisation and trade-reporting duties.
FX options not used for speculative purposes, but accepted as hedges in a treasury policy memorandum supporting underlying trade commitments.
Interest rate derivatives (e.g., EURIBOR/EURDR swap) when paired with cross-currency financing or capital-funding needs of the SARL.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Déclaration annuelle de situation (annual confirmation of RCS/INSEE company data; no change of particulars is required)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés via Infogreffe, and INSEE (Sirene)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Each calendar year between 1 January and 31 March; within 30 days of any change if a listed item changes in the year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to confirm by 31 March may generate a registrar warning; persistent failure for two consecutive years allows the register to initiate strike-off (radiation) after formal notice, and the company can be treated as no longer economically active.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Assemblée générale ordinaire annuelle (annual ordinary shareholders' meeting approving annual accounts and allocating profit)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate record; approved minutes must be available for future RCS inspections and support the accounts filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of the financial year end; for a calendar-year account, by 30 June (extensions available by court order on a reasoned application)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Any shareholder or the public prosecutor may petition the commercial court to order the meeting; failure to validly approve accounts prevents lawful dividends and may trigger judicial removal of the gérant (manager); minutes of annual meetings must be kept indefinitely.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Dépôt des comptes annuels, rapport de gestion if required, and statutory auditor's report when applicable (annual accounts filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / RCS via Infogreffe; the filing is public unless confidentiality is expressly claimed on a permitted basis
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months of the financial year end; if approved by the AGO earlier, within 1 month of approval; calendar-year accounts ordinarily due by 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: After formal notice, the court president may order filing under a coercive daily payment (astreinte); the registar may apply administrative sanctions and public registry strike-off (radiation) for a company that remains non-compliant; directors may be liable for resulting losses.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (UBO register) — annual integrity confirmation embedded in the RCS annual situation declaration; mandatory 30-day update upon any change affecting beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce / RCS via Infogreffe
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No fixed annual anniversary date; at least annually confirm accuracy through the DAS by 31 March, and file an updated declaration within 30 days of any share transfer or ownership change that alters beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-updated UBO information removes the protective effect of registration and creates criminal exposure up to 6 months' imprisonment and EUR 7,500 (approx. US$8,100) per company for the legal representative; it is not an independent strike-off trigger if the DAS is filed.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A SARL must appoint a licensed statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) if at the close of a financial year it exceeds two of the three thresholds: balance sheet total above EUR 4,000,000; net turnover above EUR 8,000,000; average headcount above 50. Below those thresholds no audit is compulsory for the marine engine manufacturing activity; shareholders may opt-in voluntarily and a court may appoint an auditor upon a justified request from members holding at least 10% of capital.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général) under the ANC's regulatory standards, derived from L.123-1 et seq. of the French Commercial Code; IFRS is not permitted for the standalone statutory SARL accounts and is reserved for consolidated accounts of listed groups.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: At incorporation the SARL files a declaration of beneficial owners with the RCS. Each share transfer or change of direct/indirect control exceeding any threshold must be reflected in the share transfer register and notified to the RCS within 30 days. There is no separate annual form absent a change; the annual Situation Declaration (DAS) filed by 31 March serves as the annual confirmation that the current UBO record is complete and accurate. Any transfer without notarial formalities must still be validated and recorded in the register before being opposable to third parties.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Registre des mouvements de titres (share transfer register, updated within one month after each transfer)
Registre des procès-verbaux et décisions des associés (shareholders' meeting minute book and written decisions)
Registre de présence et pouvoirs des assemblées (attendance and proxy records for each AGM)
Legal and accounting ledgers kept per French Commercial Code, available for inspection by auditors and judicial authorities at the registered office or via a duly designated agent

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$300–1,300 per year for third-party commercial domiciliation in a standard provincial French business centre; US$800–2,500 per year for a Paris central address with reception and mail handling; self-run physical office costs are excluded.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$6,000–25,000 for a statutory audit if the compulsory thresholds are exceeded; a non-obligatory limited review by the same licensed firm may range from US$3,500–8,000 for a small SARL.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS). Qualifying small and medium-sized enterprises may apply 15% to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit, subject to the statutory conditions, including turnover not exceeding EUR 10 million, fully paid-up share capital, and at least 75% individual ownership or qualifying ownership.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The 15% reduced rate described above is the principal general SME incentive. Other relief is conditional and activity-specific, including qualifying research and development tax credits and specified regional or investment regimes. Eligibility, state-aid limits, and notification requirements must be tested separately; no tax holiday arises solely from manufacturing engines or generators.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited carryforward period; use is generally capped each year at EUR 1 million plus 50% of taxable profit exceeding EUR 1 million. The unused balance may be carried forward. Carryback is generally available for one preceding tax year, subject to statutory conditions and a EUR 1 million cap.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD (IS return), with applicable tax-balance and installment forms 2572-SD and 2571-SD, filed electronically through the Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP) professional tax account using EDI-TDFC or the available online service. A SARL under the normal actual-profit regime generally attaches forms 2050-SD to 2059-G-SD; a simplified-regime filer uses the applicable simplified schedules.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual income tax return; corporate tax installments are generally quarterly, with statutory exceptions for newly established or low-tax-liability companies.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The IS return is generally due within three months after the fiscal year-end. For a fiscal year ending 31 December, the return is ordinarily due on the second business day following 1 May, with the DGFiP electronic-filing extension where applicable. The final IS balance is generally due by the 15th day of the fourth month after year-end (15 May for a 31 December year-end). Quarterly installments are generally due by 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, and 15 December for a calendar-year company.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2065-SD — identification and tax regime fields
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the SARL's legal name, SIREN, registered address, fiscal year dates, activity, tax office, and applicable tax regime; identify the authorized representative.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign shareholder does not change the French SARL's resident filing obligation. Use the French company's SIREN and registered-office details; do not substitute the shareholder's foreign tax number.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2065-SD — taxable result and tax computation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the tax result and applicable IS computation, including qualifying reduced-rate profit, credits, and other adjustments, consistently with the attached tax schedules and accounting records.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include income taxable to the French SARL under French law. A non-resident shareholder's own income is not reported as the SARL's taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Forms 2050-SD to 2059-G-SD, or applicable simplified schedules
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile the statutory accounts to taxable profit and disclose balance-sheet, income-statement, depreciation, provisions, tax adjustments, and relevant related-party information in the schedules applicable to the company's regime.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply French tax rules to the French entity's accounts and retain support for cross-border related-party balances, service charges, financing, royalties, and inventory or manufacturing allocations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declare the final corporate tax due after installments and eligible credits, and pay the balance by the statutory due date.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payment remains the French SARL's responsibility even where its shareholder or finance function is located abroad.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report and pay required quarterly installments, generally calculated by reference to the preceding year's tax, subject to statutory first-year and low-liability exceptions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign-owned SARL must assess installments under the same rules as other French companies and maintain evidence of payments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Submit the annual summary of the group's transfer-pricing policy and specified related-party transactions when the statutory reporting threshold is met.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include cross-border controlled transactions and identify the foreign related parties and transaction categories using the required French reporting format.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or missing returns generally attract a 10% surcharge, increasing to 40% after formal notice and potentially 80% in cases of concealed activity or other aggravated conduct. Late-payment interest is generally 0.20% per month, subject to statutory rules. Inaccurate or incomplete declarations may attract additional tax, interest, and penalties based on the conduct and circumstances. Failure to provide required transfer-pricing documentation may trigger a specific penalty, generally the greater of EUR 10,000 or 5% of the relevant reassessed profits, subject to statutory rules.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: For dividends paid by a French company to a non-resident corporate shareholder, the domestic withholding rate is generally 25%, subject to treaty reduction or exemption. A qualifying EU parent may obtain exemption under the Parent-Subsidiary Directive and French implementing rules, generally requiring a qualifying minimum holding, holding period, eligible legal form, and subject-to-tax conditions. Non-resident individual shareholders are generally subject to a different domestic rate, commonly 12.8%, subject to applicable rules and treaty relief.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, the beneficial owner should provide the French payer with the applicable treaty relief claim or prescribed certificate, including a current tax-residence certificate issued by the competent foreign tax authority, beneficial-ownership evidence, and any required ownership or holding-period evidence. The payer applies relief at source only where the statutory procedure and documentation permit; otherwise, withholding is made at the domestic rate and the recipient claims a refund from the French tax authorities using the prescribed procedure. Confirm the applicable bilateral treaty, limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose provisions, and anti-abuse rules for the recipient's specific facts.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: French domestic withholding on specified royalties and similar payments to non-residents is generally 25% of the gross amount, subject to statutory scope, exemptions, and treaty reduction. Interest paid to non-residents is generally not subject to French withholding, except for specified cases, including payments to recipients in non-cooperative jurisdictions and other statutory exceptions. Treaty rates vary by recipient jurisdiction and income category; qualifying EU royalty or interest payments may be exempt under the applicable EU directives and French implementing rules if all conditions are met.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Generally EUR 400 million in annual turnover or gross assets for the French entity, or specified group-relationship conditions involving an entity meeting that threshold, triggers full transfer-pricing documentation under Article L.13 AA of the French Tax Procedures Code. A separate annual simplified transfer-pricing declaration (Form 2257-SD) generally applies to companies meeting the relevant EUR 50 million turnover or gross-assets threshold or belonging to a qualifying group. Country-by-country reporting generally applies to qualifying multinational groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not have a general UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations regime. French tax law nevertheless requires transactions and arrangements to reflect economic reality and may deny benefits or recharacterize arrangements under domestic anti-abuse, abuse-of-law, transfer-pricing, beneficial-ownership, and EU anti-abuse rules. A French SARL should maintain commercially credible French functions, personnel, decision-making, assets, and records consistent with the risks and profits it reports.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion or fraudulent tax return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing taxable income, using knowingly false invoices, fabricating deductions, or deliberately omitting transactions to evade French tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, interest, and penalties that may reach 80% in aggravated cases; tax fraud is punishable under the French Tax Code and Penal Code, potentially by imprisonment and substantial criminal fines. Enhanced penalties may apply to organized or aggravated fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who personally participates in fraud may face criminal prosecution, imprisonment, fines, and professional consequences. Civil recovery against a director is not automatic; statutory conditions or a court finding of fraudulent or serious and repeated tax failures may permit personal recovery. Travel restrictions are not an automatic tax sanction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Pricing related-party goods, services, financing, intellectual property, or business restructurings on non-arm's-length terms, or failing to provide required documentation or a Form 2257-SD when due.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Taxable-profit adjustments, interest, and applicable penalties; failure to provide documentation when legally required may attract the specific penalty generally measured as the greater of EUR 10,000 or 5% of reassessed profits, subject to statutory provisions and procedural requirements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The company is ordinarily liable for tax and penalties. Directors may incur personal criminal or civil liability if they knowingly participate in fraud or satisfy statutory conditions for personal liability; ordinary documentation failures do not automatically pierce limited liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, royalties, or other reportable amounts to a non-resident without applying required withholding, or claiming treaty or EU relief without substantiating residence, beneficial ownership, and eligibility.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The payer may be assessed for unpaid withholding tax, interest, and applicable penalties. False certificates or sham arrangements may trigger anti-abuse reassessment and, in deliberate cases, criminal proceedings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The SARL is generally the withholding agent and primary debtor. A director's personal liability requires an applicable statutory basis or personal participation in wrongdoing; it is not automatic solely because withholding was omitted.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a company or intermediary lacking genuine commercial purpose to obtain treaty benefits, conceal the beneficial owner, shift profits artificially, or disguise the actual recipient or activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authorities may deny treaty or statutory benefits, recharacterize transactions, reassess tax, and impose interest and penalties. Deliberate fraudulent conduct may also result in criminal sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal criminal liability if they knowingly implement or facilitate fraud. Limited liability is not displaced merely because the company has limited operations; personal exposure depends on the relevant statutory test and proven conduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly handling criminal proceeds, concealing beneficial ownership, breaching applicable asset-freeze or sanctions measures, or making prohibited cross-border payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Potential criminal fines, imprisonment, asset confiscation, transaction restrictions, and administrative measures under the applicable French and EU regimes. The specific sanction depends on the offence, intent, amount, and applicable sanctions instrument.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and other responsible individuals may be prosecuted where they commit, order, or knowingly facilitate an offence. Corporate liability may coexist with individual liability; travel bans are not an automatic consequence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to maintain accounting records or make required filings
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to keep reliable statutory accounts and supporting records, filing an incomplete or late IS return, or failing to retain evidence for deductions, tax credits, and related-party transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, loss of unsupported deductions or credits, late-filing or late-payment penalties, interest, and, where facts warrant, accounting or criminal sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal consequences for intentional misconduct or specified serious breaches. Routine company tax debts and filing penalties do not automatically create personal director liability.
